title: feat(types): declare `step` on SliderFieldMetadata
body:
Fixes #10066

Clause-②: yes — this grows a published type (`@object-ui/types` `SliderFieldMetadata` gains `step`), only to match what the spec and the widget already accept.

## What changed

- `packages/types/src/field-types.ts`: `SliderFieldMetadata` declares `step?: number`, with a docblock that quotes the spec's own describe ("Step increment for slider (default: 1)").
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/number-field-step-spec-parity-9875.test.ts`: section 4 used to record the gap with a `@ts-expect-error` on `step`. That directive would now be unused, so the section is flipped into a pin of the new state:
  - `SliderFieldMetadata['step']` equals `number | undefined`.
  - An annotated `SliderFieldMetadata` literal carrying `step` compiles.
  - A misspelled key (`stpe`) sits under `@ts-expect-error`, so the excess-property check stays live.
- `packages/fields/src/widgets/SliderField.tsx`: `field as any` is replaced with a `Pick` of `SliderFieldMetadata` over `min | max | step`. The widget also serves `progress` fields (the `progress: SliderField` entry in `EDIT_WIDGETS`), so asserting the full interface, `type: 'slider'` included, would claim more than the carrier guarantees. The read line `const step = sliderField?.step ?? 1;` is byte-identical, so the source pin in the 9875 test still holds. Runtime behaviour is unchanged.
- `.changeset/10066-slider-step.md`: patch for `@object-ui/types` and `@object-ui/fields`.

## Premises measured (installed tree, worktree based at `142fdfd`)

- `SliderFieldMetadata` had `type`, `min` and `max` only. Control: `NumberFieldMetadata.step?: number` is present in the same file. The only zod `slider` hits are `SliderSchema` in `zod/form.zod.ts`, which is the form component, not a field-metadata mirror.
- Installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 has `step: z.number().optional().describe("Step increment for slider (default: 1)")` in its `dist` (24 dist files carry the string).
- `SliderField` read `step ?? 1` off `field as any` and passed `step` to `Slider`.

## Verification (code at `7ff843c`; head `a9b9cb3` adds only the changeset)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check`: exit 0. It runs `tsc --noEmit`, then `tsconfig.examples.json`, then `tsconfig.test.json`. The closure build (`@object-ui/types^...`) is empty, so pnpm reports no build script; `types` has no workspace deps. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` includes the 9875 test file.
- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/fields^...' build`: exit 0, across 10 of 47 projects. Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields type-check`: exit 0.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` on the 9875 test plus the four fields suites that name `SliderField` (`slider-signature-host-channels-e2e`, `widget-dom-leak-e2e`, `readonly-host-plumbing-e2e`, `widget-aria-invalid-registry-e2e`): Test Files 5 passed (5), Tests 415 passed (415).
- Reverse verification, run after committing: I removed `step?: number` from `SliderFieldMetadata` with an anchor-asserted replace. The on-disk count of `step?: number;` went from 2 to 1. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` then exited 2 with TS2339 (`Property 'step' does not exist on type 'SliderFieldMetadata'`) and TS2353 (object literal `step`). I restored with `git checkout HEAD --`. After that, `git diff HEAD` was empty and the file's hash matched the HEAD blob.
- eslint (`--no-inline-config`) on the 3 changed source files: 0 errors, 6 warnings. All 6 are pre-existing `no-explicit-any` on untouched lines of `field-types.ts`. `SliderField.tsx` now has 0 warnings.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0. `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: exit 0, 0 new citations. `check:changeset-claims` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`: exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- There is no field-level docs page for `slider` under `content/docs/fields/`. The `content/docs/components/form/slider.mdx` page documents the form component, not the field metadata, so no docs page was updated. This is noted here and not filed.
- `EDIT_WIDGETS` routes `progress` to `SliderField`, but `FieldMetadata` has no `progress` member. That is why the widget reads through a `Pick` rather than the full interface. It is an observation only.
